title: Princeton PEAR lab and the Global Consciousness Project: random event generators spike on 9/11 and at Bob Jahn's death

tellings.quote: 911 was the biggest spike they've ever seen.

plain: A Princeton University lab and a project that grew out of it, the Global Consciousness Project, kept machines called random event generators running. These devices spit out random numbers, and the idea behind them is that strong shared human emotion might push the numbers away from chance. Michels says the machines jumped on 9/11, "the biggest spike they've ever seen," and again when Bob Jahn, the man linked to the lab, died. He tells it himself, pointing to Jahn, and if it were true it would mean human minds can nudge physical events.
